name: Hotel Adlon Kempinski Berlin
positioning: Kempinski hotel on the Unter den Linden, directly at the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin
best_for: Travelers who want to stay directly at the Brandenburg Gate
Families who want age-appropriate gifts for children in the bedrooms

facts.text: The hotel is directly at the Brandenburg Gate.
The hotel is on the Unter den Linden boulevard in Berlin's Mitte district.
Rooms have windows that open and look out on the Brandenburg Gate.
Breakfast is served at the BeL Etage.
Brasserie Quarre has outdoor tables and serves bistro dishes such as bouillabaisse.
Guests can take an Adlon Bike to the Tiergarten park.
Children receive age-appropriate gifts in the bedrooms.
The hotel has ground-floor suites and wheelchair access points with adaptable bed levels.

highlights.text: The central elephant fountain was a gift from a visiting Maharajah at the hotel's launch in 1907.
The current hotel opened under the Kempinski name in 1997 as a symbol of German Reunification.
The hotel serves currywurst Adlon-style with gold leaf.
The spa has a Finnish sauna, a hammam, ice baths and an ice waterfall.
The hotel has original Art Deco elevator clocks that show which floor you are on, an antique from the original building.

considerations.text: The spa is a child-free zone for guests under 16.
WhataHotel notes the hotel is in a high tourist area with busy surrounding streets.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Hotel Adlon Kempinski Berlin
